newsitem.title: USA: Cool, dry weather forecast for U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Cool, dry weather forecast for U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Cool, dry weather was forecast for much of the Midwest through the weekend, which may aid planting efforts if farmers want to risk placing seeds in cool soil, meteorlogists said.
"Most of the problem with planting the crop is with cool temperatures," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Seeds will remain dormant until soil temperatures rise enought to prompt germination, Burgio said.
Forecasts called for highs from the 50s to low 60s degrees Fahrenheit through the weekend, and lows from the 30s to low 40s, with the coolest temperatures in northern areas.
Isolated showers were likely Saturday in Missouri and southern Illinois, but greater rainfall was likely Monday across the Midwest.
Burgio said 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain were likely from eastern Missouri across southern and east central Illinois, and over most of Indiana and Ohio.
"That would be the best opportunity to shut down planting," Burgio said.

Marshall Wickman, meteorologist with Wilkens Weather Technologies, said he expected the storms now in Texas and Oklahoma to slowly move northeast, reaching the Ohio River Valley Monday, with rain amounts there Monday and Tuesday of 1.0 to 2.0 inches.
